title: Hybrid fragment hedging and leaky-slab protector: adaptive eviction for high-variance KV workloads
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Introduces a hybrid eviction policy that combines slab-protection heuristics with probabilistic fragment hedging to reduce KV cache fragmentation and spill pressure. Improves tail latency under bursty, multi-tenant workloads and adds telemetry for eviction decisions.
description:
Context and motivation: Production KV cache workloads showed recurring spill spikes during tenant traffic bursts that correlated with high fragmentation and frequent micro-evictions. Existing slab allocators protect hot slots but can overprotect cold-but-long-lived fragments, causing slow compaction and elevated paging/spillback under sustained pressure. This PR introduces a hybrid approach that: (1) applies a leaky-slab protector that decays strong protection windows for low-access, long-lived fragments, and (2) performs probabilistic fragment hedging — occasional, low-cost compaction probes that reduce fragmentation entropy without stalling the allocator.

Summary of changes (single string): 1) new eviction policy module kv/evict/hybrid_hedge.cc + headers implementing HybridHedgeEvictor that composes slab-protector and probe-driven fragment hedger; 2) leaky_slab_reservation: time-decay based reservation metadata attached to slots with tunable half-life; 3) compaction probe runner: background low-priority probe worker that does non-blocking micro-compaction on fragment candidates; 4) spill smoothing: spill rate limiter that aggregates small spill events within a tenant window to avoid cascade spill; 5) observability: eviction decision traces (sampled), fragment-entropy metric, and tenant-level spill_latency histogram; 6) runtime knobs: flags to configure decay half-life, probe frequency, and spill-smoothing window exposed via config/api surface for Dedicated/Private deployments; 7) tests + bench harness: unit tests for hedging heuristics, integration test with synthetic bursty tenants, and benchmarking harness that reproduces prior spike scenario.

Commits (high-level): - aisha/hedge-init: Add HybridHedgeEvictor core algorithm and interfaces - aisha/leaky-slab: Implement time-decay reservation metadata and unit tests - aisha/probe-runner: Add non-blocking compaction probes and background runner - aisha/spill-smoother: Introduce spill rate aggregation and limiter - aisha/telemetry: Eviction tracing & fragment-entropy metrics - aisha/tests: Integration + benchmark harness reproducing spike patterns

Changed files (high-level): - kv/evict/hybrid_hedge.cc (new) - kv/evict/leaky_slab.h/.cc (new) - kv/evict/probe_runner.cc (new) - kv/evict/spill_smoother.cc (new) - runtime/config/eviction_config.proto (modified) - telemetry/metrics/evict_telemetry.cc (modified) - tests/kv/hedge_integration_test.cc (new) - bench/kv/spike_repro_harness (new)

Testing & benchmarks: Microbenchmarks against the prior baseline show: - 35-48% reduction in spill I/O in bursty tenant scenarios (95th percentile) - 12-22% improvement in 99th percentile latency for small-token inference calls impacted by KV cold faults - negligible CPU overhead (+~2% average) due to probe runner being low-priority and rate-limited. Bench harness included reproduces a 20-minute burst pattern used in oncall incident SUP-501. Integration tests added to CI reproduce non-regression for steady-state workloads.

Reviewer thread (summary): - Diego Martinez: "Initial read looks good; need to see more bench traces and a clearer safety fallback if probes start affecting tail latency." Requested targeted profiler output at initial probe frequency. Author response: uploaded flamegraphs for 5-minute probes (bench artifacts) and added a runtime safety valve that pauses probes if probe_worker_cpu > 8% or if eviction tail latency worsens for two consecutive sampling windows. - Sofia Patel: "Nice telemetry. Please make sure the fragment-entropy metric is high-cardinality safe and sampled." Requested sampling at 0.1% by default and option to increase for dedicated customers. Author updated telemetry to sample and added docs. - Marcus Lee: "Concern about release rollout and config surface; want gradual canary and strict defaults." Requested sane defaults and a rollout plan. Author added conservative defaults (probe frequency = 1/min per shard, decay half-life = 30m) and a rollout note.

CI and gating: Full CI ran (unit/integ/bench). Two intermittent flaky tests were observed on first run (tests/kv/allocator_async_test) related to timing; fixed by adding deterministic waits in probe runner startup. Final CI status: all checks passing. Bench artifacts and flamegraphs uploaded to CI artifacts and linked in PR.

Backward compatibility and safety: No surface-breaking API changes. All new knobs default to conservative values and are disabled in older config profiles. Added a feature flag hybrid_hedge_enabled=false by default for Hosted tier; enabled by default for internal Dedicated staging clusters used in benchmarks. Rollback plan: feature flag + config toggle; quick revert path is a single-commit revert for the feature gate in main if unexpected behavior occurs.

Merge and rollout: After 2 approvals and green CI, PR was squash-merged on 2024-11-20. Feature is gated behind hybrid_hedge_enabled flag; we will enable in a small Dedicated canary group for two weeks before wide rollout.

Notes for operators: - Monitor metric evict.fragment_entropy (lower is better up to a point) and spill.smoothing.window_spill_rate to detect regressions. - If 99th latency increases after enabling, set hybrid_hedge_enabled=false and open oncall ticket referencing SUP-501. - Config knobs: decay_half_life_minutes, probe_frequency_per_shard, probe_cpu_threshold_pct, spill_smoothing_window_seconds.

Why this is different from previous work: Prior PRs focused on aggressive compaction or strict slab protection. This change takes a middle-ground that hedges fragmentation with low-cost probes and lets slab protection decay so that cold long-lived fragments do not permanently starve compaction. The probabilistic probe design reduces worst-case amplification of compaction work and improves steady-state tail behavior under bursty multi-tenant traffic.

Outstanding follow-ups (todo): - Add adaptive tuning loop that adjusts probe frequency based on observed entropy slope (ENG-2193) - Evaluate combined effect with existing KV prefetch heuristics (benching scheduled) - Add tenant-prioritized pacing policy for very large tenants (separate PR)

Related work and references: SUP-501 incident on 2024-09-10, ENG-2179 spec doc linked in internal Linear board, benchmarking harness in bench/kv/spike_repro_harness.

Merge outcome: merged (squash).
